substitute.reason: referee-three failed after its one retry: ingest refused both attempts (verdict judge with a zero-width joiner)

findings.evidence: Step 1's detect-tools paragraph says 'informational only, this step does not add new wizard questions' and 'this is the data `ai-kit-spec-execute` will need later; this step only surfaces it'. It asks the agent to mention rg/sd/bat/eza/fd/codebase-memory-mcp during 'optional per-reviewer/per-executor questions later in the wizard', but no step in SKILL.md or wizard-flow.md uses that data or names that question.
findings.fix: Tie the paragraph to a named step: for example, in wizard-flow.md step 6 show the detect-tools result next to the code-index alternative line for each kept lane. If no step needs it, keep the detect-tools call, replace the paragraph with one line saying its output is saved for ai-kit-spec-execute, and record the shortened text.

findings.evidence: '`references/wizard-flow.md` sets the question order (Step 2.2); Steps 2.3 to 2.8 hold the per-topic rules it points to.' The Process pattern's numbered steps do not run in numbered order. wizard-flow.md step 5 calls Steps 2.3, 2.4 and 2.6, step 6 calls 2.5, step 7 calls 2.7 and step 11 calls 2.8. An agent reading SKILL.md top to bottom meets 2.3 to 2.8 as if they were sequential checkpoints.
findings.fix: Keep Steps 0 to 4 as the sequential checkpoints and rename Steps 2.3 to 2.8 as lookup sections (for example 'Rule: vendor attribution', 'Rule: test the pair'), with a one-line note that wizard-flow.md calls them in its own order. Change every 'Step 2.x' reference in references/*.md to match. No content is removed.

findings.evidence: 'Never re-derive the write target at Step 3' gives only '(consistency guarantee)' as its reason, and line 37's 'Never skip announcing the target path' gives only 'user must know'. Most other NEVER items name the concrete failure they prevent.
findings.fix: Give the concrete failure. Line 38: 're-deriving at Step 3 can pick another file than the one the owner's replace answer covered, for example after a cwd change or a new XDG_CONFIG_HOME, so --replace would overwrite a roster nobody approved'. Line 37: 'announced late, the owner cannot catch a wrong layer before answering a dozen questions for it'.

findings.evidence: The description is 1013 characters, 11 under the 1024 hard limit. Much of it is implementation detail rather than user intent: 'asks each role's order, effort and opt-in flags' and 'Supports --check-only (availability report, no config writes), --local and --global (pick the target, never consent to replace it)'. Any future addition will break the limit.
findings.fix: Sets up, refreshes or checks ai-kit's cross-AI lanes: which models review plans, which implement them, and each role's fallback order. Detects installed CLIs and models, proposes review and execute sets from the model catalog for the owner to pick, and writes the [lanes] roster of .aikit/config.toml (the user config with --global), asking before it replaces one. Use when the user wants cross-AI reviewers or executors added, changed, reordered or checked (--check-only), even without the word lanes; when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers reports no lanes; to find lane providers opencode no longer lists; or to migrate an old review-spec.toml. Not for running a review or execute with configured lanes, hand-editing one lane value, or editing [runner] or opencode.jsonc.

findings.evidence: The body is 419 lines and has several single paragraphs over 1,000 characters (lines 201, 203, 276, 329, 351), so it is likely well past the spec's ~5,000-token recommendation for the body. Rules also recur. The session-default ask appears at line 31, lines 312-318 and session-default.md 'Why it is always offered'. 'This test call spends part of the lane's allowance' appears at line 285 and in wizard-flow.md steps 5 and 6. The timeout_tiers sum appears in Gotchas line 54 and again at lines 339-340.
findings.fix: Move the replacement-gate detail of Step 2.1 (lines 201-203) and the check-reviewer detail of Step 2.5 (line 276) into references, for example references/write-target.md and references/test-call.md, read at those steps. Leave a two-line rule plus the read trigger in SKILL.md. Keep each repeated rule once, in the step or reference that runs it, and point to it from the NEVER and Gotchas lines. Record every moved paragraph.

findings.evidence: 'from ai_kit_spec.cli import CliDeps, _probe_lanes, _route_reviewers'. The probe preflight before a live, allowance-spending call depends on private helpers, and the file admits 'a rename there breaks it'. This conflicts with SKILL.md line 14's rule that calls go 'through the `ai-kit-spec.py` factory subcommands, never hand-typed'.
findings.fix: Add a read-only subcommand that prints the probe key list, for example 'probe-quota --list-keys --role both --no-migrate', with a script test. Replace the inline python block with that one command, and keep the existing nonzero-exit fallback text.

findings.evidence: Eval 'edge-opencode-not-installed-config-fallback' depends on 'my opencode.jsonc defines a provider called mine, and a reviewer uses mine/m', but has 'files': []. Neither the opencode.jsonc nor the reviewer config exists, so a grader cannot reproduce the 'config file only' branch. edge-sort-skills-jev-absent and edge-sort-proposal-is-advisory likewise give no classify-skills fixture.
findings.fix: Add evals/files/opencode-config-only/opencode.jsonc (provider 'mine') and evals/files/opencode-config-only/config.toml (one review lane on mine/m) and list them in that eval's files. Add a small skills fixture, or a recorded classify-skills output, for the two skill-sorting evals.

findings.evidence: 'When the user only asks to migrate an old `review-spec.toml`, report `migration pending`, say that the next command that reads the roster ... migrates it, and stop'. This branch runs before check-providers and runs no other check. Nothing tells the agent how to confirm that an old roster actually exists, or whether it is held, before reporting 'migration pending'. With no old file present, the branch still reports a pending migration.
findings.fix: In this branch, first run the read-only 'python3 "$TOOLS_PY" config-status --cwd "<project root>"' (or check-providers, which reports migration pending). Relay its 'migration pending' or 'migration-held' line. If neither appears, say there is no old review-spec.toml to migrate, then stop.

findings.evidence: 'The one exception: the user declined the test at Step 2.5's write-risk ask'. For codex and cursor, whose profiles say read_only confirmed, no write-risk ask is made. If the owner says 'skip the test' for such a lane, no branch covers it: the NEVER line forbids saving it untested, and nothing says whether to refuse, drop the lane or insist on the call.
findings.fix: Add one line to Step 2.5: on a read-only-confirmed runtime the test is not optional. If the owner refuses it, explain that the lane cannot be saved untested and offer (1) run the test, (2) drop the lane. Add an eval for that answer.
